newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy business says rate cut limited by PSBR, wages.
newsitem.headline: Italy business says rate cut limited by PSBR, wages.

text.p: Prospects of a cut in the Bank of Italy's discount rate are limited by the overshoot in the 1996 public sector deficit and the metalworkers' pay dispute, the Italian employers' organisation Confindustria said on Wednesday.
Confindustria added in its latest economic statement that there were no signs of an imminent economic upturn.

"A reduction in the discount rate appears now to be limited by the overshoot in 1996 public accounts and the outcome of the national contract negotiations in the engineering sector," its statement said.
The Treasury announced last week that Italy had run up a 1996 public sector borrowing requirement of 138.5 trillion lire, well above a revised government target of 123 trillion.

Trades unions representing 1.7 million metal and engineering workers agreed on Wednesday to unleash a fresh wave of strikes to press demands over a pay claim after talks between the government, unions and employers appeared to have broken down.
Financial markets have been expecting a cut in the central bank's 7.5 percent discount rate once the dispute has been resolved.

Confindustria said however that three-month eurolira rates "are discounting a reduction of some 150 basis points" with respect to spot rates "by the middle of the year, with 100 bps of the cut coming in the next quarter."
The negative yield curve for short-term state debt also pointed to an expected cut, it added.

But as for an economic recovery, after latest data showed a fall in industrial production in October of 0.9 percent on September, "output should show a slight rise on average in November and December," Confindustria estimates showed.
But "indicators available up to now do not show signals of an imminent recovery," the statement said.
